title: runstate v0.4 lifecycle convention
description: Pins the bodies of the lifecycle.* topics the worker produces: started (attach + self-reported liveness handle), heartbeat (tick beacon), stopped (cooperative dying breath), nak (a refused control request). Applied on top of the envelope schema. v0.4 adds a required `t` (the worker's wall-clock when it emitted the record) to started/heartbeat/stopped -- the records the observer/liveness plane reads -- so a third party that did not launch the run can date the beacon and answer staleness (docs/specs/observer-clock.md). `started.attached_at` was renamed to `t` and made required non-null in the same bump. `nak` is deliberately left undated (nothing times it).

Started.description: Pushed on attach; the worker self-reports its liveness handle (§8). t is the worker's wall-clock at attach (required non-null) -- the run epoch, and one uniform clock across the lifecycle event records. It was `attached_at` (present-nullable) before the observer-clock harmonization.

Heartbeat.description: Tick-driven liveness beacon. consumed_seq is the worker's read position in its inbound `control` order (§11-12), published after durable registration. t is the worker's wall-clock when it beat -- what lets a third-party observer date the beacon and answer staleness (observer-clock).

Stopped.description: The cooperative dying breath; its existence on the log = a clean, resumable halt (§7). completed=true is the worker's opt-in claim of intrinsic completion; otherwise the stop projects to preempted. error is the failure diagnostic; a completed stop carries no error. t is the worker's wall-clock at the dying breath (the finish time / GC-age answer).

Nak.description: A refused control request, correlated by request_id. `reason` is a closed enum: malformed (body didn't conform -- a sender bug), unsatisfiable (well-formed but provably zero fires), unsupported (unknown control verb). `message` is free human detail.
